meta.name: Build an engineering knowledge graph with ClickUp, GitHub, Claude, and Slack

parameters.content:
## AI Engineering Knowledge Graph

### How it works

This workflow continuously ingests events from ClickUp, GitHub, an incident-management tool, and a documentation platform, normalizes each into a shared graph-event format, and buffers them. On a scheduled batch window, it pulls the buffered events and extracts structured relationships wherever fields are already explicit (assignee -> task, PR author -> repo, incident -> affected service, etc.). Anything left in free text (a task description mentioning a service, a PR body mentioning an incident, a doc page referencing an API or database, a proposed architecture decision) is ambiguous and gets passed to Claude, which reads it against a snapshot of the known entity registry and extracts additional links, matching to existing nodes where possible instead of inventing duplicates. The resolved links are merged, turned into node/edge upserts, written to the graph database, and summarized in Slack.

### Setup steps

- Configure a ClickUp webhook/automation to POST task created/updated events to the ClickUp intake webhook.
- Configure a GitHub webhook (pull_request events) on the relevant repositories to POST to the GitHub intake webhook.
- Configure your incident-management tool's webhook (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or similar) to POST incident created/updated/resolved events to the incident intake webhook.
- Configure your documentation platform's webhook (Confluence, Notion, or similar) to POST page created/updated events to the docs intake webhook.
- Review and adapt each normalization Code node so incoming payload shapes map to the canonical fields used downstream (entityType, entityId, free-text fields, structured link fields).
- Add credentials and endpoint details for the graph-event buffer API used by the store and fetch HTTP Request nodes.
- Set the batch-window schedule to how often you want the graph refreshed (e.g. hourly).
- Add credentials and an endpoint for the entity registry lookup (a read endpoint on your graph store returning known developers, repos, services, APIs, databases, etc.) used to ground the AI's entity matching.
- Configure Anthropic credentials for the Claude entity-linking agent and select the intended model in the Anthropic chat model sub-node.
- Add graph-database API credentials and adjust the bulk node/edge upsert endpoint and payload shape for your store (Neo4j, Neptune, or any graph service with a bulk-upsert API).
- Connect Slack credentials and choose the channel that should receive knowledge-graph update summaries.

## ClickUp intake

Receives ClickUp task events and normalizes assignee, status, tags, and any explicit repo/service links into the shared graph-event format.

## GitHub intake

Receives pull_request webhook events and normalizes author, repository, and PR description into the shared graph-event format.

## Incident intake

Receives incident-management events and normalizes affected service, severity, and postmortem links into the shared graph-event format.

## Documentation intake

Receives documentation-platform page events, flags architecture-decision-record pages, and normalizes title/content/author into the shared graph-event format.

## Buffer normalized events

Combines the normalized events from all four intake lanes and posts each into the external buffer service for later batch processing.

## Fetch batch window

Starts the scheduled graph-update cycle and retrieves events accumulated in the buffer during the most recent processing window.

## Extract and route

Pulls out relationships already implied by structured fields as clear links, and flags any event with free text that might reference other entities as ambiguous for AI review.

## Resolve ambiguous links

Fetches a snapshot of the known entity registry for grounding, then uses a Claude-powered agent to read each ambiguous event's free text and extract additional entity relationships, matching to existing nodes where possible instead of creating duplicates. Applies the AI result back to the workflow's link structure.

## Pass clear links

Handles the links that were already explicit from structured fields, preserving them without sending them through the AI resolution branch.

## Merge link results

Recombines the AI-resolved ambiguous links and the directly passed clear links into one unified link stream.

## Write graph and notify

Builds node and edge upserts from the final links, writes them to the graph database, and summarizes the update in Slack.
